items.title: Your Bills Come Every Month. These 5 Dividend Stocks Pay That Way, Too
items.summary: Quarterly dividends leave retirees covering rent and utilities out of pocket. Five monthly payers promise to fix that, but one of them works differently from the rest, and each hides a risk that could shrink your check.

items.title: How a 66-Year-Old Collects $5,775 a Month From Just Three Tickers: JEPI, O, and ARCC
items.summary: A retirement plan that fits on one index card sounds almost too tidy. Each of its three holdings hides a weak spot, and one of them has been paying out more than it earns for three straight quarters.

items.title: A $400,000 Portfolio in Albertsons Companies, Edison International and Realty Income Pays $21,624 a Year in Dividends. Here’s What Happens if One Cuts
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA hypothetical $400,000 portfolio split evenly across Albertsons Companies, Edison International and Realty Income pays about $21,600 a year in dividends, or about $1,800 a month. Realty Income’s dividend has the least room on its own measure, at 75% of AFFO, but that’s near the low end of its history, and it raised the dividend again in November.

items.title: Investing $500 a Month in Coca-Cola, Realty Income, and Altria Could Generate Over $1,000 in Monthly Dividend Income by 2046
items.summary: As the old adage goes, slow and steady wins the race. And as another adage reminds us, quality pays for itself.

items.title: Realty Income Builds Private Capital: Can Fees Lift Earnings?
items.summary: Realty Income expands its private capital platform to boost fee income, attract institutional investors and support AFFO growth.

items.title: Investors 50 and Older Can Put $8,600 Into a Roth IRA in 2026 to Build Tax-Free Dividend Income
items.summary: Four household-name dividend stocks can quietly hand the IRS a four-figure bill every year, and one of them does most of the damage. Investors over 50 hold a special tool to fight back, but income limits can shut some couples out.

items.title: Big Yields Are Easy to Find. These 4 Dividend Stocks Cover Theirs With Cash to Spare
items.summary: A fat yield means little if the cash behind it runs thin. Four dividend payers, from a pipeline giant to a burger empire, pass a stricter test, though each carries one risk that could squeeze its next raise.

items.title: $200 a Month in Realty Income Could Generate $150 in Monthly Dividends by 2036
items.summary: Steady investment in this REIT's shares could turn it into a three-figure monthly income stream in 10 years.
